app.direct.body: Traffic leaves from the phones' IP addresses. The phones and their carriers see which addresses you connect to, and websites may see different IP addresses in one session. Use encrypted connections (HTTPS) only.
app.direct.draining: Finishing old connections now that the tunnel is back…
app.direct.title: Direct mode — no tunnel to the server.
app.notEnrolled: The hub is not enrolled on a server.
app.pending.body: The hub switched to the server from the new code and retries the enrollment through the phones until the server answers. If this takes long, check that the server is running and the code has not expired (valid 24 h).
app.pending.title: Waiting for the new server to answer.
bond.mode.maxHint: All phones together — fastest download and upload.
bond.mode.minHint: Games and calls: small packets go over the fastest phone, in two copies.
bond.pepExcludeHint: Ports, port ranges and IPv4 networks that skip acceleration
bond.pepHint: The hub and the server end TCP connections on behalf of the client, and only the data goes through the phones. Helps on links with loss and uneven latency. Running connections stay in their current mode.
bond.red.autoHint: When a link loses packets or wavers, calls and games (UDP) go in two copies.
bond.red.offHint: Every packet goes one way. Least data from the phones.
bond.red.onHint: Every packet goes two ways: resists loss, but uses 2× more data from the phones.
bond.test.atLeast: At least this much: the link took everything the test sent
bond.test.atLeastNote: ≥ — the link took everything the test sent, also in the repeat with a larger data limit, so it is at least this fast.
bond.test.cost1: The test usually uses up to
bond.test.cost2: A link faster than the first measurement shows is measured again with a larger limit — then at most
bond.test.cost3: in total. This is your friends' data — make sure they agree. During the test, the connection through this phone slows down.
bond.test.costAll: of mobile data from {n} phones ({each} MB from each)
bond.test.costOne: of mobile data of the phone {name}
bond.test.hint: Measures the raw throughput of each phone ({secs} s download + {secs} s upload).
bond.title: Bonding mode
bypass.hint: Domains (with their subdomains) and IP addresses on this list go out directly through a phone, from its carrier IP address — e.g. a bank that blocks server addresses.
bypass.label: One entry per line: a domain (bank.pl) or an IPv4 address / network (203.0.113.0/24)
bypass.noRelays: none, the traffic goes through the tunnel
bypass.stats: Addresses from DNS: {learned} · phones that can carry the traffic: {relays}
bypass.title: Bypassing the server
bypass.warn: This traffic does not go through the tunnel: the phone and its carrier see what you connect to. Use HTTPS only. Works only for devices that ask the hub's DNS for addresses.
chart.label: Throughput chart
chart.title: Throughput (5 min)
close.hint: What to do with the hub (the xs-hubd service) when you close this window.
close.pref.keep: Keep the hub running in the background
close.pref.stop: Stop the hub (the hotspot turns off)
close.title: Closing the window
closeDlg.body: The hub can keep running in the background — the hotspot and tunnel stay, and you can open the window again at any time.
closeDlg.remember: Remember the choice (change it in Settings)
closeDlg.title: Close the CrossStream Hub window?
closeDlg.warn: “Stop the hub” turns off the hotspot: connected laptops lose internet.
diag.hint: The hub's recent logs to a text file. Codes, passwords, keys, MAC addresses and public IP addresses are hidden, so the file can be sent when asking for help.
diag.title: Diagnostics
diag.verboseHint: More detail in the logs for 15 minutes, then back to normal
enroll.againToast: Hub enrolled again — the service is restarting
enroll.dialogTitle: Enroll the hub on a server
enroll.err.noAnswer: The server does not answer through this computer's connection or a local link. If the server is in the same home network, the router usually does not pass connections to its own public address (no “hairpin NAT”): add a phone and enroll the hub through it, or turn on hairpin NAT in the router. Also check that the code is new.
enroll.err.noHandshake: The server does not answer. Try again with the same code — if the server already accepted this hub, the enrollment completes. The code may also have expired (valid 24 h) or been revoked, or the server is down.
enroll.pathHint: Enrollment goes through a connected phone or an enabled local link of the hub (Panel tab); when there is none, through this computer's internet connection. Now: {phones} connected, {links} enabled.
enroll.pendingToast: The new server has not answered yet — the hub switched to it and keeps trying
enroll.step1: First add a phone: in the CrossStream Relay app tap “+ Add hub” and scan the code. The enrollment goes through its mobile network — this also works when the server is in the same home network.
enroll.switchedAs: Switched to the new server as
enroll.switchedRest: ; waiting for it to answer (the hub keeps trying).
enroll.viaComputer: No phone: the enrollment goes through this computer's internet connection. If the server is in the same home network, it may fail — then go back and add a phone.
enroll.viaLink: No phone: the enrollment goes through an enabled local link of the hub.
enroll.viaPhone: The enrollment goes through the phone ({names}).
err.daemon: The xs-hubd service is not running.
fwd.col.name: Name
fwd.hint2: leads to the same port of a device in the hub's network. Name the device by its MAC address (a DHCP IP address can change) or by its IP address. Only while the hub has a tunnel to the server.
fwd.reason.in_use: port already used by another hub
fwd.reason.not_allowed: the server allows no more ports (xs-ctl forward allow)
fwd.state.no_client: no such device on the network
fwd.title: Port forwarding
fwd.windows: Not available in the Windows hub (Mobile Hotspot cannot add forwards).
go.captive.hint: Log in to this network on a phone or turn the hub off for a moment
go.captive.open: The internet works — no login needed
go.logs.title: Save hub logs
go.mode.OFFLINE: no phones and no local links
go.notify.cap100: {mb} MB limit used up — the phone is no longer used.
go.notify.joined: The phone joined and shares data.
go.notify.weakWifi: Weak Wi-Fi signal to the hub ({dbm} dBm) — move the phone closer.
go.upd.busy: Another update installation is running (a second window or xs-hubctl update). Try when it ends.
go.upd.cannotInstall: This hub cannot install the update itself — download it from the release page.
go.upd.checkFailed: Could not check for updates (no connection to GitHub?).
go.upd.noRelease: No release has been published yet.
go.upd.rateLimited: GitHub is limiting requests from this address for now. Try again in an hour.
go.upd.stalled: Download stopped: no data came for a minute (computer asleep or network lost?). Try again.

hotspot.headless: xs-hubd runs without a hotspot (headless mode).
hotspot.restartHint: Changing the name or password restarts the hotspot — the phones must be paired again.
hotspot.savedRepair: Saved. The phones must be paired again (new QR code).
hotspot.stopWhat1: The network “{ssid}” goes away: all phones ({phones}) and devices ({devices}) are disconnected.
hotspot.stopWhat2: The hub carries no data until you start the hotspot again.
hotspot.stopWhat3: When it starts again, the phones reconnect on their own (no pairing). After a restart of the xs-hubd service the hotspot starts automatically.
hotspot.title: Wi-Fi hotspot
hotspot.why.nextTo: next to the laptop's Wi-Fi network, on its channel
lang.title: Language · Język
notify.hint: System notifications; the same event from the same phone at most once per 5 minutes. This window shows them: while it is closed (the hub runs in the background) there are none.

notify.type.cap_100: A phone's data limit used up
notify.type.relay_joined: A phone or local link joined
notify.type.relay_left: A phone or local link disconnected
own.hint: The browser and other apps on this laptop use the phones too. Open connections restart once. Without a working path the laptop uses its own links.
own.noResolved: No systemd-resolved: DNS queries go as before, outside CrossStream.

own.onToast: The laptop's traffic goes through CrossStream
own.title: This laptop's traffic through CrossStream

pair.title: Add a phone

relay.weakWifiHint: Wi-Fi phone ↔ hub: {dbm} dBm. Move the phone closer to the laptop.
relays.col.linkHint: How the phone connects to the server: UDP (best), TCP or WSS when the carrier blocks UDP
relays.none: No paired phones — scan the QR code in the CrossStream Relay app.
relays.overflow: “Secondary” phones are used only when the main ones carry less than

relays.title: Phones ({n} of {total} connected)

state.starting.body: . Starting usually takes a few to a dozen seconds (with the Windows hotspot about 10 s).
state.starting.title: Starting the xs-hubd service…
state.win.auto2: itself; starting takes up to a dozen seconds.

stats.lastTest: Last link test: {down} Mb/s download, {up} Mb/s upload.

upd.ask3: The hub service restarts: the hotspot goes away for a dozen seconds or so, the phones reconnect on their own.
upd.ask4: This window closes and opens in the new version.
upd.askPassword: The system asks for the administrator password.
upd.cannotInstall: This hub cannot install the update itself (started from outside the install folder): download it from the release page or use
upd.dev: This is a development build: it is not updated from releases.
upd.dismiss: Do not show for this version

upd.title: Updates
uplink.capError: Data limit: a whole number of MB ≥ 0
uplink.cappedHint: The link comes back in the next period or after the counter is reset (Limit…)
uplink.forgetAsk: Remove the link “{name}” from the list?
uplink.forgetBody: The hub stops using it and forgets its settings and counter. If the link is plugged in, it shows up again as new, turned off.
uplink.loginHint: Opens this network's login page (hotel, train) in the browser
uplink.loginOpened: {name}: login page opened in the browser
uplink.noInternetHint: The login page check got no answer through this link
uplink.sameIpHint: This link has the same public IP address as “{name}” — the same connection, no gain.
uplink.sameIpUsb: Turn off Wi-Fi on the phone
uplink.throttle: When over, slow down to 256 kb/s instead of turning off
uplink.ttl: Set TTL 65 (hide sharing from the carrier)
uplink.ttlHint: Carriers detect internet sharing by TTL; 65 hides the laptop behind the phone
uplink.weakCellHint: Weak modem signal or high loss. Move the laptop closer to a window.
uplinks.newOff: A new link stays off until you turn it on — data from a modem or phone is not used without consent.
uplinks.none: The laptop has no links to the internet. Connect a phone with a USB cable and turn on “USB tethering” on it (no app needed, iPhone works too), plug in Ethernet or a USB modem, or use the laptop's SIM card — they show up here.
uplinks.title: Local links ({n} of {total} active)
wifiAsk.body2: for the hotspot the phones connect to. Choose what to do — the choice is remembered (change it in Settings → Wi-Fi hotspot).
wifiAsk.cannotShare: This card cannot run a hotspot next to a network connection. Another option: a second Wi-Fi card (USB) for the hotspot.
wifiAsk.disconnectHint: The laptop leaves the network “{conn}”; its internet goes through the tunnel over the phones.
wifiAsk.shareHint: The laptop stays on this network and the hotspot runs next to it on the same channel. Not every card or channel allows this — if it fails, I ask again.
